title: Chicken Souvlaki
kicker: Lemon-oregano skewers, tzatziki with real garlic authority, and warm pita — Greece in fifteen minutes of grilling.
story: Souvlaki is Greek street food distilled: small chunks of marinated meat on skewers, grilled hard, wrapped in pita with tzatziki, tomato, and a shake of dried oregano. Where shawarma is a spice marathon, souvlaki is a sprint — lemon, garlic, oregano, olive oil, done. The marinade is simple because the grilling does the heavy lifting.

Tzatziki deserves the same respect: full-fat Greek yogurt, cucumber squeezed genuinely dry (wet tzatziki is a puddle), garlic grated to paste, dill, a thread of vinegar. Make it an hour ahead so the flavors settle. Then the only real technique left is knowing when the skewers are done — caramelized edges, springy center, juices running clear, and that instant when the grill smell makes everyone wander into the kitchen.
fun_fact: Souvlaki means 'little skewer' — the diminutive of souvla. Athens street vendors have served versions of it since at least Aristophanes, who name-dropped grilled skewers in a comedy around 400 BC.

ingredients.note: plus the grilled lemon halves at the end
Greek oregano if possible — it is a different herb

ingredients.item: sweet paprika + 1/2 tsp each salt & pepper
dill, chopped + 1 tsp red wine vinegar

steps.title: Marinate 2-8 hours
steps.text: Whisk oil, lemon, garlic, oregano, paprika, salt, pepper. Coat the chicken and refrigerate 2 hours minimum, 8 maximum — beyond that the lemon starts curing the surface.

steps.title: Tzatziki first, so it settles
steps.text: Grate cucumber, salt lightly, squeeze in a towel until almost no water remains — genuinely dry. Fold into yogurt with garlic paste, dill, vinegar, salt. Refrigerate an hour; it thickens and mellows.

steps.title: Skewer with contact
steps.text: Thread chunks so they touch but aren't crushed — packed skewers steam, loose ones dry out. If using wooden skewers, soak 30 minutes so they don't become kindling.

steps.title: Grill hot, turn once
steps.text: High heat, grill or cast-iron pan, 3-4 minutes per side, turning once or twice, until charred at edges and cooked through (74°C / 165°F internal). Total 10-12 minutes.

steps.title: The pita finale
steps.text: Warm pitas on the grill for 30 seconds per side. Wrap chicken with tzatziki, tomato, onion, and an extra drizzle of oregano oil. Charred lemon halves squeezed over everything — this is the move people remember.

notes: Thigh meat is the souvlaki standard; breast works but pull it at 70°C / 158°F to keep it from drying.
Make double tzatziki — it disappears on everything from fries to roasted vegetables.
No grill? A screaming cast-iron pan with the window cracked does a respectable job.

storage: Marinated raw chicken keeps 2 days refrigerated. Cooked chicken 4 days — great cold over salad. Tzatziki 4 days refrigerated; stir before serving.

equipment.n: soak wooden ones 30 minutes or sacrifice them
or a grill pan - the stripes are flavor
pull at 74 C, rest, be happy

facts.first_recorded: 3,600 years — stone cooking lines for skewers found at Akrotiri, Santorini
facts.name_means: Diminutive of souvla (big skewer) — 'little skewer', said with affection.
facts.technique: Lemon-oregano marinade, high fire, rest, wrap
facts.serve_at: Off the skewer, in pita, at golden hour
facts.pour: Retsina — pine resin wine, an acquired taste worth acquiring

relations.cluster_note: Same idea, two empires: the rotating shaved roast (Ottoman) versus the lemon-oregano skewer (Greek).
